status: FROZEN_AT_COMMIT (declared before its formal run; SHA-256 pinned in tests/test_rubber_p2_3_protocols.py; a change is v2)
calibration_status: SIMULATOR_ONLY_UNCALIBRATED (numerical verification of the energy books of a moving Dirichlet grip; no material data)
purpose: Prerequisite of every P2-3 test with moving grips (RUBBER-VISC hysteresis, energy balance): a moving F8 projected grip must close its energy books with the kick-average constraint work (constraint_work kick_average_v1), in the single-env reference and byte-wise in the batched path.

provenance.diagnostic_before_declaration: artifacts/rl_ready/p2_3/moving_clamp_diag_001 (scene S1 only, both profiles, CFL 0.5 / 0.25, control 100 / 25 us): kick-average residual max 0.38 % (linear) / 0.23 % (smootherstep) of S at CFL 0.5, halved at CFL 0.25; v1 end-velocity residual -19.2 % / -1.6 %, dt-independent

options.traction_work: particle_velocity_v1 (no traction group in these scenes)

common.cfl_note: CFL 0.5 = the step rule's substep count; CFL 0.25 = twice that substep count at the same control interval (LiveRubberMaterial substeps override)
common.schedule_rule: control step k (0-based) of a ramp of n steps ends at tau = (k + 1) / n; the group pose at the END of the control step is pose(s(tau)); within a control step the solver interpolates the pose linearly in the substep index (slerp for the rotation), so the prescribed velocity is constant within a control step
common.energy: E_mech = Psi + KE_particle + E_grav (segmented diagnostics, end of every control step; E_grav relative to the reference state); W = solver work (kick-average constraint work); start from rest at the reference: E_mech(0) = W(0) = 0
common.residual: r(t) = (E_mech(t) - W(t)) / S, S = max over the control-step ends of (Psi + KE_particle)
common.v1_accounting_reported: r_v1(t) = (E_mech(t) - W_v1(t)) / S with W_v1 = work_end_velocity (the tlmpm_rubber_v1 end-velocity constraint work of the same run); reported, not scored

S1.label: cantilever lift + roll (the diagnostic scene)
S1.fidelity_note: n_t 2 (reduced_fidelity: coarse_thickness_resolution); a numerics test of the constraint, not a bending observable

S2.label: wide cantilever lift + yaw (in-plane bending), n_t 3

S3.label: two-grip axial load-unload to lambda 1.2 (hysteresis-shaped, elastic), n_t 3

RUBBER-GRIP-01.name: energy books of a moving projected grip close (kick-average constraint work)
RUBBER-GRIP-01.runs: every scene x profile at CFL 0.5
RUBBER-GRIP-01.criteria: M = max_t |r(t)| <= m_max and |H| <= h_max, H = mean of r over the scene's hold window
RUBBER-GRIP-01.rationale: the remaining residual is the bounded O(dt) energy error of symplectic Euler ((dt/2) f . g; diagnostic S1 0.23-0.38 % of S); the v1 end-velocity accounting is off by 1.6-19 % in S1 (dt-independent)

RUBBER-GRIP-02.name: first-order consistency of the residual (numerical error, not a bookkeeping bias)
RUBBER-GRIP-02.runs: every scene x profile at CFL 0.5 and 0.25
RUBBER-GRIP-02.criteria: M(CFL 0.25) <= ratio_max * M(CFL 0.5), or M(CFL 0.25) <= floor
RUBBER-GRIP-02.rationale: symplectic-Euler energy error is O(dt) (ratio 0.5; diagnostic 0.49-0.50); a quadrature bias at velocity discontinuities is dt-independent (ratio ~1)

RUBBER-GRIP-03.name: validity
RUBBER-GRIP-03.criteria: invalid_reason == 0 at every control step (no NONFINITE_STATE, RUBBER_J_DOMAIN, RUBBER_CFL_EXCEEDED)

RUBBER-GRIP-04.name: batched L0 byte-wise
RUBBER-GRIP-04.runs: per scene: BatchedRubberMaterial of N = 2 (env 0 = the scene, env 1 = l0_env1: other length, mu x 1.5, rho 1050, motion amplitude x 0.7; smootherstep; both built with step_material = env 1's material) on the Warp CPU device (parity_mode) against two single-env references built identically
RUBBER-GRIP-04.criteria: after every control step of the whole schedule: every solver array of both envs (particle, node, group, traction, cell CSR, index, work, violations, cfl_violations and every option array including work_end_velocity, F64, x64 and the projection rows / blocks / inverses / scratch), the segmented diagnostics, markers and wrenches are byte-identical (same dtype, shape and raw bytes) to the single references
